data.name: MOD0001_Title
data.value: A module must not expose public types

data.name: MOD0001_Message
data.value: Type '{0}' is public in a module assembly

data.name: MOD0001_Description
data.value: A module's types are an implementation detail, and the rule that keeps the host free of module references depends on that. Make it internal, or move it to a contracts library. Controllers, page models, view components, tag helpers and configured entity types are exempt; anything else goes in fusion_modules_allowed_public_types.

data.name: MOD0002_Title
data.value: The type named by HostingStartup must be a module

data.name: MOD0002_Message
data.value: Type '{0}' is named by [assembly: HostingStartup] but does not derive from '{1}'

data.name: MOD0002_Description
data.value: ASP.NET Core instantiates this type and casts it to IHostingStartup. Deriving from ModuleBase is also what registers the module and checks that the modules it references were activated.

data.name: MOD0004_Title
data.value: The host must not use types from a module

data.name: MOD0004_Message
data.value: The host uses types from module assembly '{0}'

data.name: MOD0004_Description
data.value: A project reference is fine — it orders the build and copies the module to the output. Using the module's types is not: it puts that module in every deployment. Move the shared type to a contracts assembly.

data.name: MOD0007_Title
data.value: The host must not declare an ApplicationPart for a module

data.name: MOD0007_Message
data.value: The host declares [assembly: ApplicationPart] for module assembly '{0}'

data.name: MOD0007_Description
data.value: Application Part Discovery does not know about HostingStartup: it loads a module's controllers and pages without running the module. Set GenerateMvcApplicationPartsAssemblyAttributes to false and let each module call AddApplicationPart.

data.name: MOD0003_Title
data.value: A module must be named by an assembly-level HostingStartup attribute

data.name: MOD0003_Message
data.value: Module '{0}' is never named by an [assembly: HostingStartup] attribute and will not be loaded

data.name: MOD0003_Description
data.value: Without the attribute the module fails silently: ASP.NET Core loads the assembly, finds no attribute and moves on, so the module's services and endpoints do not exist and nothing is logged.

data.name: MOD0008_Title
data.value: A module must not replace the application pipeline

data.name: MOD0008_Message
data.value: '{0}' replaces the whole request pipeline and must not be called from a module

data.name: MOD0008_Description
data.value: IWebHostBuilder.Configure and UseStartup define the pipeline rather than adding to it, discarding whatever the host and every other module set up. Override ModuleBase.Configure instead.

data.name: MOD0009_Title
data.value: A module must not register itself as a startup filter

data.name: MOD0009_Message
data.value: '{0}' already registers itself as an IStartupFilter

data.name: MOD0009_Description
data.value: ModuleBase already registers the module as an IStartupFilter. Registering it again runs Configure twice, duplicating every piece of middleware and every endpoint the module adds.

data.name: MOD0011_Title
data.value: MVC never discovers the module's controllers or pages

data.name: MOD0011_Message
data.value: MVC never discovers {0}: {1}; every route they map answers 404

data.name: MOD0011_Description
data.value: The package stops the host from adding modules as MVC application parts (MOD0007), so each module adds its own assembly — which is also how its Razor pages and views are found — and a module's controllers are internal (MOD0001), which MVC skips unless the module calls AllowInternalControllers(). A module that does neither starts, passes its probe and answers 404. In ConfigureServices: builder.Services.AddControllers().AddApplicationPart(typeof(Module).Assembly).AllowInternalControllers().

data.name: MOD0011_NoApplicationPart
data.value: the module never adds its assembly as an application part (AddApplicationPart)

data.name: MOD0011_InternalNotAllowed
data.value: it is not public, and the module never calls AllowInternalControllers()

data.name: MOD0012_Title
data.value: The host does not validate its modules

data.name: MOD0012_Message
data.value: The builder from '{0}' is never passed to ValidateModules, so a misspelled or missing module in HOSTINGSTARTUPASSEMBLIES starts a healthy-looking application that serves 404s

data.name: MOD0012_Description
data.value: ASP.NET Core logs a critical message for a hosting startup assembly it cannot load and starts anyway. ValidateModules, generated from the host's references, fails startup instead: every name in HOSTINGSTARTUPASSEMBLIES has to load, and each of the host's modules has to have run. Call it on the builder that loads the modules: WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args).ValidateModules(), or ValidateModules() on a generic host with ConfigureWebHostDefaults or ConfigureWebHost.

data.name: MOD0006_Title
data.value: The host's builder does not load modules

data.name: MOD0006_Message
data.value: WebApplication.{0} does not run hosting startups, so no module named in HOSTINGSTARTUPASSEMBLIES is loaded; use WebApplication.CreateBuilder

data.name: MOD0006_Description
data.value: CreateSlimBuilder and CreateEmptyBuilder configure the web host without running hosting startups. HOSTINGSTARTUPASSEMBLIES is read and ignored, so every topology of the host is the host alone, with no error and no log line. Modules need WebApplication.CreateBuilder, which takes the same arguments.

data.name: MOD0010_Title
data.value: A hub's client interface must be reachable from SignalR's generated proxy

data.name: MOD0010_Message
data.value: '{0}' is the client interface of hub '{1}' and is not visible outside this assembly

data.name: MOD0010_Description
data.value: SignalR builds the proxy for a Hub<TClient> into a dynamic assembly of its own, which cannot implement an internal interface declared in yours. The project compiles, no other rule fires, and every test that never starts a hub passes; the running process throws TypeLoadException the first time it resolves IHubContext. Grant the proxy access with [assembly: InternalsVisibleTo("Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.TypedClientBuilder")], or make the interface public and follow the compiler through its signatures.

data.name: MOD0005_Title
data.value: A library that is not a module must not use types from a module

data.name: MOD0005_Message
data.value: Library '{0}' uses types from module assembly '{1}'

data.name: MOD0005_Description
data.value: A library is loaded wherever something that uses it is loaded, and the compiler makes every assembly it uses a dependency of its users. A module used by a plain library ends up in every deployment of every host or module that uses the library. Move the shared type to a contracts assembly, or make the library a module.

data.name: MOD0013_Title
data.value: The FusionModules package is not referenced

data.name: MOD0013_Message
data.value: This assembly declares a HostingStartup but does not reference '{0}', so module rules cannot be verified

data.name: MOD0013_Description
data.value: The runtime package is missing, so ModuleBase cannot be found and the rules that depend on it are inactive. The build is green because nothing is being checked.

data.name: MOD0014_Title
data.value: Two modules register one service with different implementations

data.name: MOD0014_Message
data.value: Modules register '{0}' with different implementations ({1}); where they are loaded together, only one registration is resolved and the other module gets an implementation it did not register

data.name: MOD0014_Description
data.value: Each service had a container of its own before the merge; now the modules share one, and for a service resolved as one instance the last registration wins (or the first, with TryAdd). Register a keyed service, or a service type of each module's own. If the type is consumed as IEnumerable<T>, put an attribute named MultipleImplementationsAttribute on it. If the modules are alternatives that no topology loads together, or the type is not yours, list it in fusion_modules_allowed_service_collisions; that silences this build check only. A type that is not yours and is read as a sequence by modules that do run together also needs FusionModules:AllowedServiceCollisions in the host's configuration, for the startup check. Only registrations written in the modules' own code are seen; the startup check also sees those made inside libraries.
